It is said: sala yasalu, like khafa yakhafu (meaning "sala yasalu," lightening the hamza and making it an alif).

It is also said that it is from sayl (flowing), and al-sa'il is a valley among the valleys of Hell. This is narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The first view is more sound.

The meaning of the verse is: a questioner asked about a punishment ﴿that is to occur﴾, descending and befalling those upon whom it will be sent, and for whom that punishment is. Then Allah, explaining and answering that questioner, said: ﴿for the disbelievers﴾. This is because when the Prophet ﷺ warned the people of Mecca of the punishment, some of them said to others: "Who is this punishment for, and to whom will it come? Ask Muhammad about it." So they asked him, and Allah revealed: "A questioner asked about a punishment that is to occur, for the disbelievers," meaning: it is for the disbelievers. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

It is also said that the ba' is extra (ṣila), and the meaning of the verse is: a caller called and a questioner asked for a punishment that is to occur for the disbelievers, meaning: upon the disbelievers, with the lam meaning "upon." This was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, when he invoked a curse upon himself and asked for the punishment, saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You..." (the verse) [al-Anfal: 32]. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 70, verses 3–4:**

﴿From God, Lord of the ascents.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, Lord of the heavens. He called them "ascents" (ma'arij) because the angels ascend through them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Lord of the degrees." Qatada said: "Lord of the bounties and blessings." [And "ma'arij" means: the angels.] [[The words between the brackets are an addition from manuscript "b".]]

﴿The angels ascend﴾: Al-Kisa'i read "yaʿruju" (يَعْرُجُ) with the yā' (the masculine form), which is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The others read "ta'ruju" (تَعْرُجُ) with the tā'. ﴿And the Spirit﴾: meaning Jibril (peace be upon him). ﴿To Him﴾: that is, to God, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿In a day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: of the years of this world, [if someone other than the angel were to ascend]. That is because they ascend from the lowest part of the seventh earth to the final point of God's command above the seventh heaven.

Layth narrated from Mujahid that its measure is fifty thousand years [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 29/71.]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: If the children of Adam were to travel from this world to the place of the Throne, they would travel for fifty thousand years of the years of this world.

Ikrima and Qatada said: It is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan also said: It is the Day of Resurrection. He meant that their standing for reckoning, until judgement is passed among people, lasts fifty thousand years of the years of this world. He does not mean that this is its length alone and nothing else, because the Day of Resurrection has a beginning but no end, since it is an extended day; if it had an end, it would be cut off.

Ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is the Day of Resurrection, which will be for the disbelievers the measure of fifty thousand years [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 29/71. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (4/420) attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim, and he cited four opinions on the meaning of "in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years," so consult it. The author of al-Durr al-Manthur (8/279) attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur.]].

Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Isma'il al-Tamimi informed us; Abu al-Qasim Hamza ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi informed us; Abu Ahmad 'Abdullah ibn 'Adi al-Hafiz (the memoriser of hadith) informed us; 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us; Asad ibn Musa narrated to us; Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning "a day whose measure is fifty thousand years": "How long this day is!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it will be made so light for the believer that it will be lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prayed in the world" [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 29/72; Imam Ahmad: 3/75; Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an, p. 638; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/129. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (4/420) and said that Darraj and his shaykh are weak.]].

It was also said: Its meaning is that if anyone other than God were to take charge of reckoning the servants on that day, it would not be finished in fifty thousand years. This is the meaning of the statement of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas and of Muqatil. 'Ata' said: God will finish it in the length of half a day of the days of this world.

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated from al-Kalbi, who said: He says: If I were to entrust the reckoning of that day to the angels, the jinn and humankind, and enable them to reckon, they would not finish it until after fifty thousand years, whereas I will finish it in one [single] hour [[Omitted from manuscript "b".]] of the day.

Yaman said: It is the Day of Resurrection, in which there are fifty stations, each station a thousand years. And there is inversion in the verse, as if he said: There is no repeller for it from God, Lord of the ascents, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, when the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 70, verses 5–9:

﴿So be patient with gracious patience.﴾ O Muhammad, bear patiently their denial; and this was before he was commanded to fight.

﴿Indeed, they see it as distant﴾ meaning the punishment, ﴿but We see it as near.﴾ Because what is coming is near.

﴿On the Day when the sky will be like molten brass.﴾ Like the dregs of olive oil (al-muhl). And al-Hasan said: like molten silver when it is melted.

﴿And the mountains will be like wool.﴾ Like dyed wool. ʿIhn is only said of dyed wool. Muqatil said: like carded wool. And al-Hasan said: like red wool, which is the weakest kind of wool. The mountains first change into shifting sand, then into carded wool, and then they become scattered dust.

The meaning is: no close friend will be asked about another close friend, that is, no one will be told, "Where is your friend?" The others read it with a fatha on the yā', meaning: no close relative will ask another close relative, because he is occupied with his own affair.

﴿They will be shown them﴾: they will see them. In the Resurrection, every created being, among jinn and humans, will be within sight of its companion. ﴿The guilty one would love﴾: the polytheist would wish, ﴿to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his children﴾, ﴿and his spouse﴾ (his wife), ﴿and his brother﴾, ﴿and his kinsfolk﴾ (his 'ashīrah), ﴿who separated from him﴾. Then he began, saying: ﴿Indeed, We created them from that which they know﴾, meaning: from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh. It was also said: its meaning is: "Indeed We created them [for the sake of what they do, which is the command, the prohibition, the reward and the punishment]."

It was also said: "ma" here means "man" (those who), its figurative sense being: "Indeed We created them from those who know and understand, not like the beasts." [[The words in the parentheses are omitted in "A".]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 70, verses 40–44:**

﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests.﴾ He means the rising point of each day of the year and its setting point. ﴿Indeed We are able﴾ ﴿to replace them with better than them﴾, meaning to create people better than them and more obedient to Allah [and His Messenger] [[Addition from "ب".]]. ﴿And We are not to be outdone.﴾ ﴿So leave them to wade in their falsehood﴾ ﴿and to play﴾ in their worldly life ﴿until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ It was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of fighting.

﴿The Day they will emerge from the graves﴾, from the tombs, ﴿hastening﴾ to answer the caller. ﴿As if they were rushing to a target (nusub)﴾. Ibn 'Amir [and Ibn 'Abbas] [[Addition from "أ".]] and Hafs recited "nusub" with a damma on the nun and the sad. The others recited it with a fatha on the nun and a sukun on the sad, meaning "to a thing that is set up", as in the saying: "So-and-so is set up before my eyes." Al-Kalbi said: "to a banner or flag." As for the one who recited it with a damma, Muqatil and al-Kisa'i said: it means to their idols which they used to worship besides Allah, [like His saying: "and what is sacrificed on the stone altars" (al-Ma'idah: 3)] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "أ".]]. Al-Hasan said: they will hasten toward them, each wanting to touch them first. ﴿Rushing﴾ means they hasten.

﴿Humbled﴾, abased and submissive, ﴿their eyes downcast, covered by humiliation﴾; disgrace overwhelms them. ﴿That is the Day they were promised﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection.
